intent: Changed the sensor spread from ±0.02 m to ±0.03 m (five sensors, 15 mm pitch), keeping sensor size, lead (y = 0.05), body, wheels, and mass unchanged. I expect line_loss_events to drop and max_error to fall below the 0.06 m off-track limit on at least some tracks, which should raise progress. I am considering a shorter sensor lead (y about 0.06 to 0.07) only if steering_oscillation rises at speed in the next race. I am not committing to it yet.
learning: Off-track endings at max_error about 0.06 with 1 to 2 line-loss events mean that line loss happens before the robot recovers. The next race should show whether the wider spread keeps the line in view during drift. If line_loss_events fall but max_error stays at the limit, the cause is more likely controller gain or base_speed than sensor coverage, and the geometry should be held.
rationale: The race evidence (entityR2A) shows every trial on every development track ended off_track, with zero completions. Mean max_error is about 0.062 to 0.063 m, which sits at the 0.06 m off-track limit, so the robot is drifting out to the edge and leaving. Line-loss events average 1 to 2 per run, meaning all five sensors lost the tape during the drift. With sensors at x = -0.02 to +0.02 and 12 mm footprints, the array can only see the tape while the robot is within roughly 3 to 4 cm of the centre line. Once it drifts past that, the signal drops out. The Integrator's advice is conditional: widen the spread to about ±0.03 if line loss or max_error is high in bends. Both are high, so I am taking that advice. Steering oscillation is modest (0.11 to 0.16) and does not clearly point to the sensor lead, so I am holding the lead at y = 0.05 for now. Changing both the lead and the spread at once would make it hard to tell which change helped. I am changing only the spread: five sensors at x = -0.03, -0.015, 0, +0.015, +0.03, keeping 12 mm footprints and y = 0.05. The 15 mm pitch still gives partial overlap with the 25 mm tape near centre, and the outer sensors catch drift earlier. Body, wheel, and mass values are unchanged, because the off-track limit is already at its 0.06 m floor for every allowed body_width, so widening the body gives no benefit. I expect fewer line-loss events and a lower max_error, which should lift progress above the current 0.12 to 0.19 range. Completions are not yet assured.
